title: Stylized fantasy
summary: A coherent fantasy visual language built from deliberate shape hierarchy, controlled surface detail, expressive color, and readable motion.

designKnowledge.shapeLanguage: Choose a small set of primary shapes for the world and factions; repeat them in architecture, props, creatures, and UI while varying silhouette by role.
designKnowledge.proportions: Exaggerate only where it improves role recognition or emotion. Maintain scale references for characters, doors, landmarks, and combat reach.
designKnowledge.silhouette: Test major forms as flat shapes at gameplay camera distance. Hero silhouettes must remain distinctive in the lowest certified visual tier.
designKnowledge.palette: Assign palette roles for world, faction, danger, reward, and interaction. Do not use color as the only signal for rarity, ownership, or threat.
designKnowledge.materialsAndLighting: Use a limited authored material vocabulary. Use lighting to guide navigation and mood while preserving character and objective readability on mobile.
designKnowledge.motionAndInterface: Use clear poses and restrained effects that leave gameplay silhouettes visible. Carry shape, palette, and icon motifs into UI and audio without reducing usability.

technicalPatterns.name: Style bible before asset volume
technicalPatterns.guidance: Approve a small color, shape, material, lighting, and scale sheet, then review one representative environment asset, character, UI element, and effect before scaling.

technicalPatterns.name: Quality tiers preserve identity
technicalPatterns.guidance: Lower tiers may reduce geometry, textures, effects, and environmental density, but preserve hero silhouette, navigation cues, visual identity, and gameplay readability.

dependencies.rationale: Animation pose and effect language must match the visual identity while preserving gameplay readability.
The style must be validated on the certified mobile baseline and desktop before quality tiers are accepted.

failureModes.description: Assets are individually attractive but do not share shape, material, palette, or scale rules.
failureModes.mitigation: Review representative assets together against a style bible and record explicit visual acceptance.

failureModes.description: Mobile reductions remove silhouettes, contrast, or landmarks that identify the experience.
failureModes.mitigation: Compare tiers using gameplay-distance captures and task readability checks.

scenarios.action: Review character, landmark, prop, UI, and VFX samples together at gameplay camera scale.
scenarios.expected: A reviewer can identify repeated style rules and distinguish each asset's gameplay role.

scenarios.action: Compare low and high device tiers during navigation and combat.
scenarios.expected: Essential silhouettes, objectives, and visual identity remain recognizable.

acceptanceCriteria: A style bible covers the full visual system.
Hero assets receive explicit human visual approval.
Tier changes preserve essential silhouette, readability, and identity.

considerations: Profile actual texture, mesh, lighting, and effect cost on the selected midrange mobile baseline.
A style label or editor appearance does not establish performance suitability.

sourceRefs.title: Approved Lab creative production and quality-tier requirements

evidence.description: A style production specification, tier-preservation rules, failure modes, and review scenarios are defined.

assumptions: This is one style direction and not a universal Lab style.
Specific palette and asset proportions must be authored for the selected experience.
